notes:
Judi Iranyi Photographs of the Tenderloin (SFP 179) — 528 records, and the **newest material in the archive by two decades**: every one is dated "between 2014 to 2016", so every finding here is `circa` over a three-year range and none of them can ever be sharper.

**This collection was read because #217 decided it was not what the dossier said it was.** It had been written off with SFP 130 as a Tenderloin tenant collection whose captions name living people. Measured, its addressed half is shopfronts — Daldas Grocery at 200 Eddy, Radman's Produce Market at 201 Turk, Angkor Laundromat at 353 Eddy, Hotel Essex at 684 Ellis — and where a person is in the frame the caption does not name them: "Barista behind the counter of Cafecito at 406 Ellis Street", "Tenderloin barber standing in doorway of Eddy Barber Shop". The limit bars naming a person, not photographing one. Exactly one caption in the collection names anybody at a number, by forename, and it is withheld in `raw.text` by hand — `redact` cannot reach it, because the cataloguer filed no personal subject heading and it wears no honorific.

**Two thirds of its reported address count was one phrase.** "4 Corner Friday" is a weekly street event at Golden Gate and Leavenworth, and its "4" parses as a house number on all 100 records that name it — in three spellings, so `NOT_A_STREET_PREFIX` matches the front of the name rather than the whole of it. Measured both ways before it was wired: over 57,467 harvested records the only typeless street names beginning "CORNER" are those three, all here; over every findings file in the repository, nothing committed moves. The collection's real addressed count is 51, not 151.

**An organisation named after a street number it is not at.** 826 Valencia's Tenderloin writing centre is at 180 Golden Gate Avenue, and the extractor takes the *first* number it can parse, so "826 Valencia Writing Center at 180 Golden Gate Avenue" resolved to Valencia Street. Refusing the name in `NOT_A_STREET_NAME` stops the wrong address but does not reach the right one — `address_from_title` gives up on a refused name rather than trying the next match — so sfp-179-0029 is entered by hand. A fall-through variant was written and measured: it changes 29 records corpus-wide and 27 of those are regressions, because cutting the title at the match loses the caption's own qualifier and "Rear of 80 Clara Street" becomes "80 Clara Street". Not wired.

**One placement was demoted by hand.** EAS holds 353 EDDY ST but files no parcel on it, so it was placed by point, in 0338020 — a parcel whose own range is 365-365 and with 0338021 (355 Eddy) numerically in between. The point and the block's number line disagree and that is recorded, not adjudicated. 289 Eddy is the same shape and was kept: it is the immediate neighbour of 291 with no parcel in between, which is the ordinary incomplete-range case.

**`named-buildings-only` kept 6 names and dropped 25**, and most of the 25 are real businesses — Daldas Grocery, Angkor Laundromat, El Castillito Taqueria, Em's Barber Shop, Casbah Cafe, Downtown Grocery, All Stars Donuts & Burgers, Yemen Kitchen, De Marillac Academy, Faithful Fools, the Kelly Cullen Community. They are put back by hand at publication, one page at a time, which is the tail batch's trade and is affordable at 51 records. The strict filter is what keeps "Supervisor Jane Kim speaking to others" and the barbers and baristas out.

**Two pages already carried a 1966 photograph of the same building** — the Hotel Essex at 684 Ellis and the Hotel Hamlin at 385 Eddy, both from SFH 371. `--overlap` flagged them at 36% on wording. Both were kept and worded as continuity: the hotel still trading under that name half a century later is the fact the second photograph adds.

coverage.remaining: Nothing in SFP 179; all 528 records read. What is left in the archive is SFP 136 (30 addressed), undecided and unmeasured under #217, and SFP 130 (184), closed unread by the same issue.
coverage.note: 528 catalogue records, every one read. 487 give no street number and are skipped per COLLECTION_UNNUMBERED_POLICY — the neighbourhood's street life, which is also where the collection's people are. 3 are photographs of people and never reached the address test. 38 candidate addresses became 28 findings over 28 distinct addresses, 10 duplicate records folded in; a 29th was added by hand for 180 Golden Gate Avenue. 25 resolved, 4 unresolved, 0 rejected. 25 published on 24 pages, 9 of them seeded by this run. The 100 "4 Corner Friday" records never became candidates.
